title: Redeem Telstra Plus Points for Prime Membership: 12000 Points 3 Months, 24000 Points 6 Months, 32000 Points 12 Months @ Telstra
body:
Deal: Redeem Telstra Plus Points for Prime Membership: 12000 Points 3 Months, 24000 Points 6 Months, 32000 Points 12 Months @ Telstra

[cloudie9] Need more compensation for the down time today!
[Sezza] i actually noticed this deal on the weekend but couldn't redeem it for the discounted points. It kept coming up as the normal points once i clicked through. I thought i should try again after today's issues, to see if it's fixed this bug, and now the click through with this discounted rate is working.
Hope it's helpful for anyone with points to use up!
[k0nz] Do you need to be a new member or do you receive some sort of activation code that extends out your current membership?
[Sezza] I actually was on a trial membership. It asked me whether i still wanted to activate it anyway. I did and it cancelled the trial. I'm not sure if the same thing will happen to any existing paid membership.
You might need to look at the t&cs on the telstra page.
[superm86] tnc: if you are an existing Prime member, your selected Prime membership period (3, 6, or 12 months) from Telstra Plus will be added to your Amazon.com.au account. Your existing Prime membership will be temporarily paused when the new period activates and will automatically resume once your selected period ends.
confusing
[nadan] Dang 960 points short of 32k for 12 months.
[hashtagbargain] Can you try making a prepayment to your account? Assuming points earned is based on $ spent on your account.
[nadan] I couldn't find an option to prepay, you can only topup a prepaid service.
[avinit86] Tried to redeem - took me to Amazon - not eligible for this account
Now I lost my points. Dang
[Carrera1963] You can redeem the Telstra code once your current membership runs out.
Or ask on chat for a points refund.
[karnage1020] I had the same thing back in February! Still trying to get them to refund my points … been an absolutely hilarious experience with Telstra saying it's an Amazon issue and Amazon saying it's a Telstra issue. Spoke to someone in Telstra last week and his initial reaction was "That ticket number was opened in February, are you sure you've given me the correct number?".
Anyway, long story but essentially, if you have an existing Amazon Prime membership that was obtained via Telstra points, then you can't claim the voucher until your Amazon subscription expires. It says that your existing Amazon subscription will pause, but that is only if your existing Amazon subscription was one you purchased through Amazon directly. If you have an Amazon subscription via the Telstra Plus points, the activation will fail. Unfortunate that that wasn't made clear at the time of purchase.
As long as you still have an active Telstra Service, then you should be able to redeem the voucher when your Amazon subscription expires by going to the "Manage" page on the Telstra Plus site (hub.telstra.com.au/dashboard - there should be a Manage tab at the top). In there you should see the link to redeem your subscription.
If you are like me, and no longer have an active Telstra account, then seems you are out of luck and have to just keep trying to get them to refund your points. I've been trying to get a refund since April (which is when I realised that my voucher has disappeared because I no longer have an active Telstra service).
[rpb] Activate a prepaid service on long expiry? You can even activate the $15 one on long expiry. Get a new number and also get a $10 JB perks voucher and a free GG burrito
[karnage1020] I asked Telstra Support if that would work and they assured me that it wouldn't. They even asked the Telstra Plus team who also confirmed it wouldn't work.
But I think I'll just give it a go and see.
[bwatt72] How to you know your eligible and not sure what they mean your current Amazon account paused and new account.
First off am I eligible and as a current prime member can I get this and what happens to my current.
